I am 66 years old, been farming these 15 mu in Quzhou since I was 21. Never spent a day in school. Everything I know I learned from my father and from watching the neighbors. Me and my old woman, just two mouths now. We keep 10 mu in wheat and corn, swapping every season, and 5 mu in cotton. That's the way it's been for years.

The wheat went in last October. Now it's March and the wheat is waking up. I pull my cart to the field and spread half a bag of urea on every mu — that's 25 kg of white granules. Last fall I already spread one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu when I sowed. So the wheat gets fed well. I water four times for sure: green-up, jointing, heading, and grain-filling. The pump costs diesel money, but dry wheat is thin wheat. I spray twice — once when the aphids show up, once before heading for rust. Everyone uses the same improved seed, the short kind that don't fall over. If the weather holds, I get about 550 kg per mu.

Soon as the wheat comes off in June, I hire the rotary tiller from the village — 30 yuan per mu — and tear the stubble under that same afternoon. Then plant hybrid corn. The dealer brings the seed in bright bags, and I buy what Lao Wang buys. I put 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu in the rows at planting — that's most of a bag — then topdress 20 kg urea when the corn reaches my knee. Water twice: after planting and when the tassels silk, unless heaven sends rain. Two sprays. I expect 650 kg per mu.

For cotton, I plough the 5 mu deep in late April. Cotton is hungry for potash. I spread one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu, plus I sprinkle extra potassium chloride, about 10 kg per mu. Urea goes down twice — at planting and at first flower — totaling about 18 kg nitrogen per mu. Water three times heavy: planting, flowering, and boll-setting. Three sprays for aphids and worms. I plant improved cotton seed, the kind with some bug-killer bred in. Hope to pick 350 kg of seed cotton per mu.

I count every yuan. Fertilizer is expensive this year. But I would rather put down an extra half bag than risk a thin harvest. A bad year means borrowing money. I do what I did last year, and I do what the neighbors do. If everyone around me waters four times, I water four times. Change is for young people who can afford to lose.
